landing.guides_intro: Longer answers to the questions people ask before choosing a habit app.

faq.q: Is HabitFlame free?
faq.a: Yes. The free version tracks up to 5 habits with every tracking type, streaks, badges, widgets, reminders, the focus timer, iCloud sync, Apple Health and an accountability partner with 3 nudges a month. Premium is a one-time purchase of $9.99 that removes the habit limit and adds habit stacking, smart insights, real-time partner updates and unlimited nudges.

faq.q: Do I need an account?
faq.a: No. HabitFlame works the moment you open it. Your data lives on your device and syncs through your own iCloud. Pairing with a partner uses an invite link, not a username or password.

faq.q: Which devices does it run on?
faq.a: HabitFlame is an iPhone and iPad app from the App Store. There is no Android or web version.

faq.q: Does my partner need to pay?
faq.a: No. Both people can use the free version. Real-time partner updates and unlimited nudges are Premium features on the side of the person who buys them.

pages.title: Habit tracker with an accountability partner
pages.description: A habit tracker where a friend or partner sees each habit you complete, reacts and can nudge you. How HabitFlame's accountability partner works.
pages.h1: A habit tracker with a real accountability partner
pages.deck: Most habit apps track. HabitFlame adds the one thing that changes whether you show up: another person who can see whether you did.

blocks.h2: Why a partner beats a reminder

blocks.p: A reminder tells you what to do. It does not care if you ignore it. A person does. When you know your sister will see that you skipped your walk again, the walk gets taken. That social pull is the reason running clubs, study groups and gym buddies work, and it is the reason most solo habit apps get deleted after a few weeks.

HabitFlame was built to put that pull inside a habit tracker without turning it into a social network. There is no feed of strangers, no public profile and no score to compare against people you do not know. There is one partner, or a few, and the habits you choose to share with each of them.

You add a partner from the Partners tab and send them an invite link by message, email or any share sheet destination. When they open the link in HabitFlame, the two of you are paired. If they do not have the app yet, the link takes them to the App Store first. No usernames, no passwords and no account sign-up on either side.

For each partner you decide which habits to share. Share everything, or only the one habit you keep failing at. Your partner sees the shared habits, whether you completed them today and your streak on each. Your unshared habits stay private.

ul: See your shared habits and whether each one is done today.
React to a completion to say well done, which shows up in your activity feed.
Send you a nudge when a habit is still open, which arrives as a notification on your phone.
Keep their own habits in the same app, so the accountability runs both ways.

blocks.p: Free accounts can send 3 nudges a month, enough to feel the feature. Premium removes the limit, so a partner who wants to poke you every evening can.

With Premium, real-time partner updates send your partner an instant notification the moment you complete a shared habit, and you get the same when they complete theirs. That is the version most people picture when they hear accountability partner: your phone buzzes, it says they did their workout, and now it is your turn. Without Premium, your partner's progress still shows in the app and in the partner widget when you open them, it just does not push to you at the moment it happens.

A home screen widget shows how your partner's day is going next to your own. It is a small thing, but seeing an unfinished day on someone you care about, right on your home screen, tends to end with a nudge and a completed habit on both sides.

HabitFlame does not require an account, and your habit data lives on your device and in your own iCloud. Pairing with a partner shares only the habits you pick and only their completion status, streak and reactions. There is no location sharing, no message history and nothing your partner can see beyond what you chose to share.

The partner feature sits on top of a full habit tracker. You can log a habit as yes or no, as a count such as glasses of water, as a duration such as minutes of reading, or as a multi check-in for something you do 2 to 4 times a day. Each habit runs every day, on specific days of the week or against a weekly target. Streaks, milestone celebrations, 16 achievement badges, home and lock screen widgets, a Pomodoro focus timer, stats with a full year view, and reminders that change their wording are all included.

The best accountability partner is not the most motivated person you know. It is someone who will actually notice, and who you would feel a little awkward letting down. A friend who checks their phone every evening beats a coach you speak to once a month. A sibling, a housemate or a colleague building the same kind of habit all work well.

Agree on the rules before you start. Decide which habits you will share, whether nudges are welcome every day or only when a streak is at risk, and what counts as done. A habit like reading for 30 minutes is clear. A habit like eating better is not, and a vague habit is hard for anyone to hold you to. Start with one or two shared habits, get a few weeks of streaks behind you, then add more.
Premium is a single purchase, not a subscription. Buy it once and it stays unlocked.

faq.q: Does my accountability partner need to buy Premium?
faq.a: No. Both of you can use the free version and pair. Premium only changes what the person who bought it gets: unlimited habits, unlimited nudges, real-time partner updates, habit stacking and smart insights.

faq.q: Can I have more than one accountability partner?
faq.a: Yes. You can pair with several people and choose which habits each of them sees.

faq.q: What does my partner see?
faq.a: Only the habits you share with them: whether each is done today, your streak on it, and reactions and nudges between you. Habits you do not share stay private.

faq.q: Does my partner have to be on iPhone?
faq.a: Yes. HabitFlame is an iPhone and iPad app, so both people need an Apple device with the app installed.

faq.q: What happens if my partner does not open the invite?
faq.a: Nothing changes on your side. Your habits keep tracking as normal, and you can resend the link or invite someone else.

pages.title: Streak tracker app for iPhone
pages.description: HabitFlame is a streak tracker for iPhone with milestone celebrations, a full year view and a partner who sees your streak. How streaks are counted.
pages.h1: A streak tracker that makes the chain worth keeping
pages.deck: A streak is the simplest motivator there is: a number that only goes up if you show up today. HabitFlame counts it for every habit, celebrates the milestones and lets someone else watch it grow.

blocks.p: Every habit in HabitFlame has a current streak and a longest streak. Complete the habit on a day it is scheduled and the current streak goes up by one. Miss a scheduled day and it resets, while the longest streak stays as your record to beat. Days when the habit is not scheduled do not count against you, so a habit set to weekdays keeps its streak over the weekend.

That scheduling detail matters more than it sounds. A lot of streak apps assume every habit is daily, which punishes you for a rest day you planned. HabitFlame lets each habit run every day, on specific days of the week, or as a weekly target such as 3 workouts a week, and the streak follows that rule.

Reaching a milestone streak gets a celebration on screen. The milestones are 7, 14, 21, 30, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200, 365, 500 and 1000 days. The early ones come fast on purpose: the first week is where most habits die, so the app makes a point of marking it.
Alongside streaks there are 16 achievement badges for things like your first completed week, a perfect month or a long run on a single habit. They live on the stats screen and fill in over time.

The stats tab has a full year grid, one square per day, coloured by how much of your day you completed. Weekly and monthly charts show completion rates, and each habit has its own history with current and longest streak. It is the view people screenshot at the end of the year.

Home screen and lock screen widgets show today's habits, your progress for the day and your current streaks, and home screen widgets let you complete a habit without opening the app. On a day when you are about to break a long streak, that number on the home screen is the reminder that works.

blocks.h2: A streak someone else can see

blocks.p: This is what makes HabitFlame different from a plain streak counter. Pair with a partner by sending an invite link, choose which habits to share, and they see your streak on each shared habit. They can react when you complete a habit and nudge you when a day is still open. When the streak is on the line, knowing your partner will see it break is usually enough to keep it.
With Premium, real-time partner updates notify your partner the moment you complete a shared habit. Without it, your progress still shows in their app and in the partner widget.

blocks.h2: Tracking types that fit real habits

ul: Yes or no, for habits like flossing or making the bed.
Count, for glasses of water, pages read or reps done, with a daily goal.
Duration, for minutes of meditation, practice or exercise.
Multi check-in, for habits you do 2 to 4 times a day, such as taking medication morning and evening.

blocks.p: A count or duration habit counts toward the streak once the daily goal is reached, so the streak reflects the habit you actually set, not a single tap.

blocks.h2: How to protect a long streak

blocks.p: Streaks rarely break on a hard day. They break on an ordinary day, when the habit slips your mind until it is too late. A few settings make that much less likely.

ul: Set the reminder for the part of the day when you actually have room for the habit, not the time you wish you did.
Put a widget on the home screen or lock screen, so today's open habits are in front of you every time you pick up the phone.
Schedule the habit honestly. If you only run on weekdays, set it to specific days, and the weekend will not cost you the streak.
Share the habit with a partner, who can see when it is still open and send a nudge before the day ends.

blocks.p: It also helps to keep the daily goal small enough to hit on a bad day. If the goal is 30 minutes of reading and you keep missing it, lower the goal until you can reach it on your worst day. A streak built on a goal you can hit on your worst day lasts far longer than one built on your best, and you can raise the goal once the habit has settled.
When a streak does break, the longest streak stays on record. Starting again from day one is not a failure. It is the next attempt at a number you already know you can reach.

Streaks, milestones, badges, the year view, widgets, reminders, the focus timer, all four tracking types, iCloud sync and an accountability partner are all in the free version, for up to 5 habits. Premium is a one-time purchase of $9.99 that adds unlimited habits, habit stacking, smart insights, real-time partner updates and unlimited partner nudges. There is no subscription.

faq.q: Does a rest day break my streak?
faq.a: Not if the habit is scheduled around it. Set the habit to specific days or to a weekly target and unscheduled days are skipped, not counted as misses.

faq.q: What happens when a streak breaks?
faq.a: The current streak resets to zero and starts again with your next completion. Your longest streak is kept as a record.

faq.q: Can I see streaks for more than one habit at once?
faq.a: Yes. The Today tab shows each habit's current streak, the stats tab lists current and longest streaks for every habit, and widgets show streaks on the home screen.

faq.q: Is the streak tracker free?
faq.a: Yes. Streaks, milestones, badges and the year view are all in the free version. Premium removes the 5 habit limit and adds features like habit stacking and real-time partner updates.

pages.title: Pomodoro habit app: focus timer and habit tracker
pages.description: HabitFlame pairs a Pomodoro focus timer with a habit tracker on iPhone: 25 minute sessions, timed breaks and a Live Activity, then log the minutes.
pages.h1: A Pomodoro timer inside your habit tracker
pages.deck: Some habits need a box of time, not a checkbox. HabitFlame keeps a Pomodoro timer one tap away on the Today tab, so reading, studying or deep work gets its 25 minutes, and you log the minutes on your habit when you are done.

blocks.h2: Why a timer and a tracker belong together

blocks.p: People usually run two apps: one that counts the streak, one that counts the minutes. Switching between them is where the habit slips. You finish a focus session in one app and forget to log it in the other, or you tick the habit without doing the work. Keeping the timer and the tracker in the same app shrinks that gap to a few seconds.

In HabitFlame the focus timer opens from a button on the Today tab. The timer and your habits stay separate: the timer keeps the time, and when you finish, you log the minutes on your duration habit yourself. Logging it yourself means you record what you actually did, and the streak, the stats and your accountability partner all see the same completion.

The timer follows the classic Pomodoro rhythm: a 25 minute work session, then a 5 minute short break, with a 15 minute long break after a set of 4 sessions. The screen shows the time remaining and which phase you are in, and a row of dots shows how many sessions of the set you have completed. Breaks are timed too, so you come back on time instead of drifting.

Start a session and switch to another app, and the countdown keeps running. The timer shows on the lock screen as a Live Activity, so you can see the time left without opening the app, and you get a notification when a work session or a break ends.

ul: 25 minute work sessions with a visible countdown.
5 minute short breaks between sessions.
A 15 minute long break after a set of 4 sessions.
Dots that show how many sessions of the set are done.
A Live Activity on the lock screen and a notification when each phase ends.

blocks.p: The timer pairs best with duration habits: habits you track in minutes, such as reading, language practice, writing, studying or an instrument. Set the daily goal in minutes, run sessions until you have done the time, then log the minutes on the habit. The streak counts the day once the goal is met. One 25 minute session covers a goal of 25 minutes, and 2 sessions with a break between them cover a goal of 50.
Yes or no habits can use the timer too when you want a fixed block, for example a tidy up or a planning session. Run a session, then tick the habit when the block is done.
The timer works best with a little structure around it. This routine suits most study, writing or practice habits.

ul: Decide on the task before you press start. Starting is easier when you know exactly what the first 25 minutes are for.
Put the phone face down once the session is running. The Live Activity and the notification will tell you when it ends.
Take the break properly. Stand up, get water, look away from the screen. The 5 minutes are part of the method, not time lost.
After the last session, log the minutes on your habit straight away, while the session is fresh.
Stop at the end of a set rather than pushing on through the long break. Coming back fresh tomorrow keeps a streak going longer than one heroic day.

blocks.p: If 25 minutes feels long at first, give the habit a goal of one session a day. Once that is steady for a week or two, raise the daily goal and add a second session.

blocks.h2: Keeping focus honest with a partner

blocks.p: A timer does not know whether you were working. A partner is harder to fool. Share your study or writing habit with an accountability partner, and they see whether it got done today and what your streak is. They can react when you complete it and nudge you when it is still open in the evening. With Premium, real-time partner updates notify them the moment you complete it.

The focus timer sits inside a full habit tracker. Habits can be yes or no, a count, a duration, or a multi check-in for something you do 2 to 4 times a day, and each can run every day, on specific days or against a weekly target. Streaks with milestone celebrations, 16 achievement badges, home and lock screen widgets, reminders whose wording changes and a stats tab with a full year view are all included.

The focus timer is in the free version, along with 5 habits, every tracking type, streaks, widgets, reminders, iCloud sync and an accountability partner with 3 nudges a month. Premium is a one-time $9.99 purchase that adds unlimited habits, habit stacking, smart insights, real-time partner updates and unlimited partner nudges. No subscription.

faq.q: Where do I find the focus timer?
faq.a: Open the Today tab and tap the focus timer button. The timer is not tied to a particular habit, so you can use it for any block of focused time.

faq.q: Can I change the session length?
faq.a: The timer runs the standard Pomodoro lengths: 25 minute sessions, 5 minute short breaks and a 15 minute long break.

faq.q: Does the timer log the habit for me?
faq.a: No. The timer keeps the time and the habit keeps the record. When you finish, log the minutes on your duration habit yourself, and they count toward its daily goal and the streak.

faq.q: Is the focus timer a Premium feature?
faq.a: No. The timer is included in the free version.

faq.q: Does the timer keep running if I leave the app?
faq.a: Yes. Start a session, switch apps, and the countdown continues. It shows on the lock screen as a Live Activity, and you are notified when a session or a break ends.

pages.title: Habit app for couples and partners
pages.description: A habit app two people can use together. Pair with your partner in HabitFlame, share the habits you choose, react to each other's wins and nudge each other.
pages.h1: A habit app for couples who want to keep each other honest
pages.deck: Building a habit next to someone you live with is easier when the app knows about both of you. HabitFlame pairs two people, shows each what the other completed and keeps everything else separate.
pages.faq_heading: Questions about using HabitFlame as a couple

blocks.p: HabitFlame does not merge your habits into a shared list. You each keep your own tracker, your own streaks and your own reminders. Pairing adds a window between the two: the habits you choose to share show up on your partner's phone, and theirs show up on yours.

That design fits how couples actually build habits. One of you wants to run three times a week, the other wants to read before bed. Neither habit belongs to both of you, but you both want to know the other is keeping at it.

One person adds a partner from the Partners tab and sends the invite link. The other opens it in HabitFlame and the two phones are paired. If your partner does not have the app yet, the link sends them to the App Store first. No account is created and no password is shared.
Then each of you picks the habits to share. You can share everything, or keep some habits private. A habit you do not share is invisible to your partner.

blocks.h2: What you see of each other

ul: Each shared habit and whether it is done today.
The streak on each shared habit.
Reactions on completions, so a finished workout gets a well done.
Nudges, which arrive as a notification when a habit is still open.

blocks.p: Free accounts can send 3 nudges a month each. Premium makes nudges unlimited on the side of whoever buys it, so an evening reminder from your partner can be a daily thing.

With Premium, real-time partner updates send your partner an instant notification when you complete a shared habit. If you are trying to build the same habit at the same time, say a morning walk, that ping is the small competitive nudge that gets the second person out of the door. Without Premium, your partner's progress still appears in the app and in the partner widget when they look.

blocks.h2: Habits that work well for two

ul: A shared goal done separately, such as both walking every day, each tracked on your own phone.
A habit only one of you is building, where the other is the support.
A household habit, such as a weekly tidy or a no takeout weeknight, set as a weekly target.
A health habit with a count, such as glasses of water or medication taken morning and evening as a multi check-in.

blocks.p: Pairing shares only what you choose: which shared habits are done, your streak on them and the reactions and nudges between you. There is no location, no message thread and no access to habits you kept private. Your data lives on your device and in your own iCloud, and either of you can remove the partner at any time.

Every habit can be yes or no, a count, a duration or a multi check-in for something you do 2 to 4 times a day, scheduled every day, on specific days or as a weekly target. Streaks with milestone celebrations, 16 achievement badges, home and lock screen widgets including a partner widget, reminders with changing wording, a Pomodoro focus timer and a stats tab with a full year view are all part of the app.
Pairing works best when it feels like encouragement, not surveillance. A few habits make the difference between a partner who helps and one who nags.

ul: Agree on nudges up front. Some people want one every evening, others only when a streak is at risk.
React to the wins, not just the misses. A well done on a completed habit does more than a nudge on a skipped one.
Share the habits you want help with. Keeping a habit private is fine, and it does not have to mean anything.
Talk about a broken streak in person, not through the app. The app shows what happened. The conversation is where you work out why.

blocks.p: If one of you loses interest, that is fine too. Either person can remove the partner from the Partners tab, and each of you keeps your own tracker and history.

Both of you can use the free version, which includes 5 habits each, all tracking types, streaks, widgets, the timer and pairing with 3 nudges a month. Premium is a one-time $9.99 purchase per person, not a subscription, and adds unlimited habits, habit stacking, smart insights, real-time partner updates and unlimited nudges. One of you can buy it and the other stay free.

faq.q: Do both of us need to pay?
faq.a: No. Both can use the free version and pair. Premium is bought per person and only changes the features of the person who bought it.

faq.q: Can we share the same habit?
faq.a: You each create the habit on your own phone and share it with the other. Each person keeps their own streak, and you both see whether the other completed it today.

faq.q: Can I keep some habits private from my partner?
faq.a: Yes. You choose which habits to share with each partner. Anything not shared is invisible to them.

faq.q: What if we break up or stop sharing?
faq.a: Either person can remove the partner from the Partners tab. Your own habits and history stay on your phone.

faq.q: Does it work for roommates or friends too?
faq.a: Yes. Pairing works the same for any two people, and you can pair with more than one person.

pages.title: Daily habit tracker with reminders
pages.description: A daily habit tracker for iPhone with a reminder time per habit, wording that changes, widgets and a partner who notices when you skip a day.
pages.h1: A daily habit tracker with reminders that do not go stale
pages.deck: The first reminder works. The fortieth identical one gets swiped away. HabitFlame gives every habit its own reminder time, varies the wording, and backs it up with widgets and a partner who can see the day is still open.
pages.faq_heading: Questions about reminders and the daily view

blocks.p: Each habit has its own reminder time. Set the water reminder for mid morning, the reading reminder for after dinner and the stretch reminder for right before bed. For a habit set to specific days, the reminder follows that schedule, so a habit set to weekdays does not ring on Saturday. A weekly target habit can be done on any day of the week, so it reminds you every day at its reminder time.

A notification you have seen fifty times stops being a notification. HabitFlame rotates the wording of each reminder, so the message on Tuesday is not the message from Monday. It is a small change that keeps the alert readable for longer than the first week.

blocks.h2: Choosing a reminder time that works

blocks.p: The best reminder time is not the moment you intend to do the habit. It is a few minutes before a moment you already have. Tie the reminder to something that happens every day anyway: after the morning coffee, when you get home, after dinner, before you brush your teeth. The reminder then lands when you are able to act on it, instead of in the middle of a meeting.

If you keep swiping a reminder away, move it rather than ignoring it. A reminder you dismiss every day teaches you to dismiss it. Try a later time for a week and see whether the habit starts getting done.

The Today tab lists the habits due today. Each row shows the habit, its streak and a control that matches its type: a tick for yes or no habits, a counter for counts, a timer field for durations and a set of check-ins for multi check-in habits. You can hide completed habits so only what is left stays on screen, and finishing every habit for the day gets a celebration.

Notifications are only one way to be reminded. Home screen and lock screen widgets show today's habits and how many are done, and home screen widgets let you complete a habit without opening the app. For many people the widget on the lock screen does more than the alert, because it is there every time the phone is picked up.

The strongest reminder is a person. Pair with an accountability partner, share the habits you keep skipping, and they see when a habit is still open. They can nudge you, which arrives as a notification from someone who actually cares whether you did it. Free accounts include 3 nudges a month, and Premium makes them unlimited.

blocks.h2: Four ways to track a daily habit

ul: Yes or no, for a single daily action.
Count, with a daily goal, for water, pages or reps.
Duration, in minutes, for meditation, practice or exercise.
Multi check-in, for habits done 2 to 4 times a day, such as medication or brushing.

blocks.p: Every habit can run every day, on specific days of the week, or against a weekly target such as 3 times a week. Streaks follow the schedule, so a planned day off does not break the chain.

blocks.h2: Building a daily routine that lasts

blocks.p: Start with fewer habits than you think you can handle. Two or three daily habits you finish every day build more momentum than eight you finish half of. Once the first few feel automatic, add the next one.

Keep each habit specific enough that there is no doubt about whether it happened. A count habit for glasses of water, or 30 minutes of reading as a duration habit, leaves no room for argument. A habit like be healthier cannot be ticked honestly on any day, so it quietly stops being tracked.
On a day when everything goes wrong, do the smallest honest version of each habit rather than skipping it. A short walk is still a walk, and it keeps you in the rhythm of showing up.

Every completion feeds the stats tab: weekly and monthly completion rates, a full year grid with one square per day, and current and longest streaks for each habit. Milestones at 7, 14, 21, 30, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200, 365, 500 and 1000 days get a celebration, and 16 achievement badges fill in over time. Premium adds smart insights, which look at your history on the device and point out your most consistent and most fragile habits, your best day for each habit and weekday versus weekend patterns.

Reminders, the Today view, widgets, all four tracking types, streaks, the focus timer, iCloud sync and an accountability partner are all free, for up to 5 habits. Premium is a one-time $9.99 purchase, not a subscription, and adds unlimited habits, habit stacking, smart insights, real-time partner updates and unlimited partner nudges.

faq.q: Can I set more than one reminder time for a habit?
faq.a: Each habit has one reminder time. For something you do several times a day, use a multi check-in habit, which tracks 2 to 4 check-ins, and place the reminder at the time you are most likely to forget.

faq.q: Do reminders ring on days a habit is not scheduled?
faq.a: Not for habits set to specific days: their reminders only ring on the days you picked. A weekly target habit can be completed on any day, so its reminder rings every day at the time you set.

faq.q: Can I complete a habit from the notification or widget?
faq.a: Yes. Home screen widgets let you complete a habit without opening the app, and a habit reminder has a Mark Complete action. Lock screen widgets show today's habits and your progress.

faq.q: Does the app need an account for reminders?
faq.a: No. Reminders are local to your phone, and the app never asks you to sign up.

faq.q: Can I hide habits I have already finished?
faq.a: Yes. Completed habits can be hidden from the Today tab, so the list shows only what is still open.

pages.title: HabitFlame vs HabitShare: habit tracking with a partner
pages.description: HabitShare and HabitFlame both let a friend see your habits. Where they differ: platforms, price, timer, widgets, nudges and how recently each app was updated.
pages.deck: Both apps start from the same idea: a habit is easier to keep when a friend can see it. Here is where they differ, stated as plainly as we can, so you can pick the one that fits.

blocks.p: HabitShare is free, runs on iPhone and Android, and is built around sharing habits with friends who can comment on your days and message you. HabitFlame runs on iPhone and iPad, is free for 5 habits with a one-time $9.99 Premium unlock, and pairs you with a partner who sees the habits you share, reacts to completions and nudges you when a day is still open. HabitFlame also brings a streak tracker with milestone celebrations, a Pomodoro focus timer, home and lock screen widgets and a full year view.
If one of you is on Android, HabitShare is the app that works for both of you. If you are both on iPhone and want the streak and timer side as well as the partner, keep reading.

ul: You choose which friends see each habit, and a habit you do not share stays private.
Your friend sees whether you did the habit, not just that you have an app.
Both are free to download and use.

blocks.p: HabitShare is on the App Store for iPhone and iPad and on Google Play for Android, so a pair with one iPhone and one Android phone can use it together. HabitFlame is an iPhone and iPad app only, and both partners need to be on an Apple device. That single fact decides it for a lot of couples and friends, so it comes first.

HabitShare is free and lists no in-app purchases on the App Store. HabitFlame is free for up to 5 habits with the partner, streaks, widgets, reminders and the focus timer included, and Premium is a one-time purchase of $9.99 that adds unlimited habits, habit stacking, smart insights, real-time partner updates and unlimited partner nudges. There is no subscription in HabitFlame, and both partners can stay on the free version.

In HabitShare you add friends, pick which habits each friend can see, and they follow your progress. HabitShare includes messaging and daily comments, so the accountability can turn into a conversation inside the app.

In HabitFlame you pair with a partner by sending an invite link, pick the habits to share, and they see whether each is done today and your streak on it. Instead of a message thread there are two deliberate actions: a reaction on a completion, and a nudge when a habit is still open, which arrives as a notification. Free accounts can send 3 nudges a month, and Premium makes nudges unlimited. With Premium, real-time partner updates notify your partner the moment you complete a shared habit. The absence of a message thread in HabitFlame is a design choice: the app stays a tracker, and the conversation happens wherever you already talk.

blocks.h2: What HabitFlame has that HabitShare does not list

ul: A Pomodoro focus timer with 25 minute sessions, 5 minute short breaks and a 15 minute long break.
Home screen and lock screen widgets, including a partner widget, with completion from the home screen widget.
Streak milestones at 7, 14, 21, 30, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200, 365, 500 and 1000 days, and 16 achievement badges.
A stats tab with weekly and monthly completion rates and a full year grid.
Four tracking types: yes or no, count, duration and multi check-in for habits done 2 to 4 times a day.
Reminders whose wording changes from day to day, Apple Health, iCloud sync and export.

blocks.p: The list is drawn from each app's App Store listing and website. A feature that HabitShare has but does not describe there would not appear here.

blocks.h2: What HabitShare has that HabitFlame does not

ul: An Android version of HabitShare, so mixed pairs can use it.
In-app messaging and daily comments between friends in HabitShare.
No paid tier at all, where HabitFlame limits the free version to 5 habits.

blocks.p: The HabitShare iPhone app was last updated in January 2023, according to its App Store listing. HabitFlame was updated in September 2026. That is not a statement about quality, only about how recently each app has changed, which matters for compatibility with new iPhones and new versions of iOS.

HabitFlame

Home and lock screen, plus a partner widget

ul: Pick HabitShare if either of you is on Android, or if you want to message inside the habit app.
Pick HabitFlame if you are both on iPhone and want streak milestones, a focus timer and widgets alongside the partner, with a one-time price instead of nothing at all.
Pick either if what you need is simply a friend who can see whether you did the thing. Both do that.

faq.q: Is HabitFlame free like HabitShare?
faq.a: HabitFlame is free for up to 5 habits, including the partner feature, streaks, widgets, reminders and the focus timer. Premium is a one-time $9.99 purchase for unlimited habits, habit stacking, smart insights, real-time partner updates and unlimited nudges. HabitShare is free with no paid tier listed.

faq.q: Does HabitFlame have messaging like HabitShare?
faq.a: No. HabitFlame keeps the partner feature to reactions and nudges, and leaves the conversation to wherever you already talk. HabitShare includes messaging and comments.

faq.q: Can a friend without an iPhone pair with me in HabitFlame?
faq.a: No. HabitFlame is an iPhone and iPad app, so both people need an Apple device. HabitShare has an Android version.

faq.q: Can I use both apps?
faq.a: Yes. Nothing stops you from tracking in one and sharing in the other, though most people settle on one so the streak lives in one place.
